newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr falls in Tokyo after Japan trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr falls in Tokyo after Japan trade data.

text.p: *Dollar edged down against the yen in early Tokyo partly in reaction to rise in Japan's trade surplus with the United States in March, which rose 11.2 percent from a year earlier to 379.83 billion yen, dealers said.
*Japanese interbank dealers and speculators, joined by U.S. operators, were behind dollar sales.
*But support seen near 125.50 yen with steady bids.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus slid 26.8 percent in March from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen.
*Dollar briefly inched up following smaller-than-expected overall Japanese customs-cleared trade surplus, but failed to move above 126 yen with offers lined up around that level.
*"The dollar is likely to range from 125.50 to 126 yen during the morning session now," a city bank dealer said.
*Dealers said persistent buying interest from Japanese investors near and below 125.50 yen making dollar's downside solid.
*Comments from Japanese and U.S. authorities on Wednesday still having impact and fuelling intervention fears in Asia, weighing on dollar, dealers said.

*Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, said on Wednesday that recent yen movements were clearly excessive. He added Japan will intervene in foreign exchange markets when appropriate and when it can be effective. "We will intervene when we think we can win," he said.

*The city bank dealer said Sakakibara's comments made traders wary of possible intervention around current currency levels. But a long-term credit bank dealer said intervention would not take place any time soon because it would not be effective, as traders have not accumulated long positions.

*One trust bank dealer said he would closely watch moves in Japanese market interest rates after Sakakibara said on Wednesday that there was political pressure to raise Japan's official discount rate. "If Japanese interest rates rise sharply, that could be a yen-buying factor," the dealer said.

*Wednesday remarks by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky that United States was concerned about trade imbalance with Japan and that Washington did not wish to see gap grow wider seen weighing on dollar.
*Focus on U.S. international trade figures for February at 1230 GMT. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8584
